targets.authors: Moseley GL, Olthof N, Venema A, Don S, Wijers M et al.
targets.title: Psychologically induced cooling of a specific body part caused by the illusory ownership of an artificial counterpart.
targets.evidence_quote: We set out to replicate the psychologically induced cooling of the stimulated hand during the RHI reported by Moseley et al. [ 2 ] in three consecutive experiments, comparing different experimental procedures.
targets.outcome_quote: While we could not replicate the results at all with the automated stroking procedure (used in [ 13 ]), it was possible to replicate the result using a manual stroking procedure, albeit in both the experimental and the control condition.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly contrast unsuccessful automated replications with a successful manual cooling effect, qualified by cooling also occurring in the control condition. All three experiments target the same original paper.

reasoning: New participants in each of three experiments retest the specified Moseley experiments. Other cooling studies and RHI measures are background or procedural comparisons, not independently retested targets.
